prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Yes We Can—win the best for Scotland. The SNP’s 1997 manifesto is a confident, costed plan to end Westminster’s stale, failing politics and use Scotland’s wealth for Scotland’s people through independence in Europe.

Core case and route: Scotland is a rich nation—when North Sea output is counted, among the world’s most prosperous—and has been a net contributor to the UK. Independence is normal for nations our size, and would mean automatic EU membership, open borders with England, protected pensions, and modern, non-nuclear defence. A majority of SNP MPs would trigger negotiations with the UK and EU, followed within 6–12 months by a simple referendum on the independence settlement and then fresh elections.

Democracy and rights: An independent Scotland will have a written constitution and Bill of Rights—citizens, not subjects—with protections for free expression, housing, education, free health care, decent work and a minimum wage. A single-chamber Parliament elected by proportional representation (votes at 16), entrenched local government (also PR), modernised monarchy, and strong public participation.

Economy and fair taxation: The goal is full employment, rising investment, low inflation and international credibility. The SNP will create 100,000 jobs and repay national debt while cutting business taxes to drive growth: reduce corporation tax (including a bigger cut for small firms), abolish Class IV NICs, reform business rates, boost exports, R&D and tourism, and clamp down on unfair practices. Adopt the EU Social Chapter, guarantee trade union rights, and introduce a minimum wage through consensus. Personal tax will be fair and progressive: a 15p starter rate, a broader basic band, removal of the NI ceiling, and a cut in VAT on fuel to 5%. Most Scots will pay less, the best-off a little more.

Social justice and safety: Raise child benefit, restore benefits for 16–17-year-olds, increase pensions, introduce a cold climate allowance, remove standing charges for utilities for pensioners, and abolish means testing for residential elderly care. Rebuild a real National Health Service—end the internal market, reintegrate dentistry, add resources, audit quality, ban tobacco advertising, and establish a powerful independent Food and Consumer Health Agency. Tackle crime with zero-tolerance of community offences, smarter courts and prosecution, effective alternatives to prison, a serious drugs strategy, and a total handgun ban.

Education and housing: Hire more teachers, repair schools, wire classrooms and guarantee free nursery places for 3–4-year-olds; restore student grants and expand high-quality training and apprenticeships. Transform housing by transferring most council housing debt to free investment: build social homes, renovate and insulate, protect new stock from discounted right-to-buy, and replace Scottish Homes with an accountable agency.

Nationwide renewal: Abolish feudal tenure and open up land ownership; empower communities and councils over shore and seabed. Revive agriculture (traceability, CAP refocus), double woodland cover, support crofting, reform fisheries management and strengthen processing. Protect the environment (independent SEPA, national targets). End nuclear reprocessing, pivot Dounreay to decommissioning and renewables R&D. Secure Scotland’s fair share of North Sea assets, end gas-pricing discrimination, phase out nuclear power and build renewables. Create an integrated transport system—invest in rail, bring Scottish Railtrack assets into public ownership, remove bridge tolls, fix Highlands and Islands air duty—and extend world-class telecoms and digital access.

Europe, world and defence: Be a full EU member with votes, veto, and a turn at the Presidency; build targeted global diplomacy; join the UN, Commonwealth and Council of Europe; create professional Scottish Defence Forces, remove Trident, move out of NATO’s nuclear posture, champion peacekeeping, and meet the UN aid target over six years.

This is fully costed. If the SNP wins, so does Scotland. Yes We Can.
